transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-08
Start: 16:30 PST
Duration: ~59 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees (Redwood): Samira Patel (AE), Liam O'Connor (SE), Priya Nair (CSM)
Attendees (DeltaOps): Rajiv Menon (CTO), Maya Collins (DevOps), Ethan Park (ML), Sofia Torres (Security), Grace Liu (Product)

Summary:
High-level kickoff for DeltaOps implementation of Redwood inference platform. Primary goals: run a 6-week pilot for customer-facing chat and embeddings, evaluate private VPC deployment with KMS integration, and measure latency/unit-cost targets. Discussed networking, security, rollback/rollout plan, and pilot success criteria. Some transcription noise and mis-recognitions throughout.

Topics covered:
- Pilot scope and success metrics (latency tail, cost per 1k tokens, embedding throughput)
- Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Security: SSO/SAML, SOC2 artifacts, KMS/HSM integration, data retention
- Infra intake: network, certificates, egress rules, NAT/peering
- Observability and rollouts: canary, fallback, tracing hooks
- Next steps and owners

Action items recapped at end (also in metadata).

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samira with Redwood Inference, AE on this account. quick round robin?
[00:14] Rajiv: Rajiv here, CTO at DeltaOps, thanks. we're trying to move from a mixed in-house stack to something more predictable for inference costs.
[00:28] Maya: Maya, DevOps, I'll own the VPC/network part.
[00:33] Ethan: Ethan, ML, i'll handle the model/eval side.
[00:38] Sofia: Sofia, security, i'll ask the hard questions.
[00:42] Liam: Liam, SE at Redwood, I'll walk through the deployment options and infra intake.
[00:48] Priya: Priya from CS, i'll be your onboarding contact and timeline owner.

[01:05] Liam: Ok cool, quick agenda. pilot length we usually see 4-8 weeks; propose 6 weeks. goals: two endpoints — chat generation for customer support triage, and embeddings for semantic search. target p95 latency under 350ms for chat (for 512 tokens) and embedding throughput 10k requests/day initially. is that roughly aligned?
[01:35] Ethan: Yep that's our baseline. current in-house 90th is like 800ms and cost is spiking with spikes.
[01:43] Rajiv: cost stability is the big driver, also compliance — some of our data is regulated in EU.

[02:02] Samira: Great. deployment decision: for pilot we recommend private VPC with Redwood Private control plane — gives you KMS integration and no customer data egress to public internet. but we can start with Hosted to get quick time-to-value. tradeoff is latency/cost and speed.
[02:25] Maya: Quick question — how strict is the VPC peering? we typically block public IPs, need all egress through our NAT.
[02:33] Liam: You can do VPC peering or private link; we support peering and transit gateways depending on cloud. we'll put together a network intake checklist. note: if you choose Hosted with VPC peering, some networking changes needed but faster to start.
[02:50] Sofia: From security, we need SOC2 artifacts, SAML SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration where customer owns keys. can you support HSM-backed key stores?
[03:05] Samira: Yes we support customer-managed KMS and HSM via our Private offering. we have SOC2 Type II report available, and SAML SSO with SCIM for user provisioning. i'll share the security pack.
[03:20] Sofia: Great. also, data retention and raw transcript storage, do you persist PII anywhere?
[03:28] Priya: by default logs are retained for 30 days in hosted. for Private you control retention and can disable long-term retention of raw payloads. we'll document retention settings.

[03:50] [04:02] Ethan: technical — model selection. we plan to run an instruct-style LLM for chat plus sentence-transformer-like model for embeddings. do you host open models or do we bring our own?
[04:16] Liam: We have a catalog of curated open models and can host customer models. for pilot we can bring a reference LLM (gpt-like open checkpoint) and do a side-by-side with your current model. note on quantization: lower precision can drastically reduce cost but may affect output quality; we'll recommend quant profiles per workload.
[04:40] Ethan: Are kv cache and prefix caching supported? we heavily rely on context caching for session-based chat.
[04:48] Liam: Yes, KV cache management and prefix caching are supported, we call out K V cash in some older notes haha, transcription always messes that up. caching reduces token cost and latency for repeated contexts.

[05:10] Rajiv: curious about throughput scaling — we have spiky traffic (seasonal). how does Redwood Dedicated behave with bursts?
[05:22] Samira: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with burst capacity options; plus autoscaling policies. for pilot we size a dedicated pool for baseline and allow burst via hosted fallback. that gives SLA-backed throughput for steady load and flexible capacity for peaks.
[05:40] Maya: What about canary/rollback if a model regression happens during rollout? we need automatic fallback.
[05:48] Liam: Redwood's rollout supports canary percentages and automatic fallback to a previous model variant if quality or latency regressions are detected. we also integrate with your eval harness if you provide it.

[06:12] Sofia: Encryption in transit and at rest — do you support customer TLS certs, and API keys rotation?
[06:20] Priya: yes to both. TLS for private endpoints, plus short-lived tokens for service accounts and KMS for encrypted at-rest keys. we'll include cert rotation guidance.

[07:00] [07:28] Grace: timeline — we want customer-facing pilot in production by end of Q1. is that doable?
[07:36] Samira: Q1 production target is feasible with a 6-week pilot and then a 4-week production ramp if we avoid major infra blockers. key dependencies: network peering, KMS access, and sample traffic for sizing.
[07:55] Rajiv: we'll need cost modeling — want to see hosted vs dedicated TCO.
[08:02] Samira: we'll provide a pilot pricing worksheet. for modeling we need token mix, seq length distribution, and concurrency estimates. can you share that?
[08:14] Ethan: yes i'll export our 7-day traces and a sample prompt set.

[09:00] [09:22] Liam: on observability — Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model. you'll get tracing hooks and per-request IDs to tie to your logs. note some customers still send logs to their splunk/datadog via forwarding.
[09:40] Maya: forwarding - network egress again. we prefer to keep data in our logging cluster; will need to open specific egress endpoints.
[09:51] Liam: noted, we'll include end-to-end networking details.

[10:15] [10:30] Rajiv: security review — can you run a short threat model workshop with our security folks? maybe a 60-min session.
[10:38] Sofia: yes please, we'll invite cloud security and compliance.
[10:43] Priya: we'll schedule that as a separate call, include SOC2 artifacts and KMS runbook.

[11:05] [11:30] Ethan: about model artifacts — how do you handle model version pinning and rollbacks? we need reproducible model hashes for audits.
[11:38] Liam: models are versioned and you can pin by model id and model hash. rollouts can be done by version and we maintain an audit trail for each request and model hash.

[12:12] [12:35] Grace: do you support latency SLOs per route?
[12:40] Samira: yes, per-route latency and per-token cost metrics are configurable in the Console. for Dedicated customers we also offer SLA-backed latency targets in contracts.

[13:00] [13:25] Maya: we have internal networking constraints: only outbound to specific IPs allowed, and all traffic must egress through our firewall. will Redwood provide IP ranges?
[13:33] Liam: yes we provide a list of IP ranges for peering and egress; for Private deployments you won't need public egress.

[14:10] [14:38] Sofia: compliance — do you have EU data residency options?
[14:44] Samira: yes, we have regions in EU and you can restrict routing to EU-only. for Private you can run in your on-prem infra if needed.

[15:00] [15:24] Rajiv: small concern — we've been talking to Anthropic and they pitched a simpler hosted flow. what's the differentiator here?
[15:34] Samira: main diff is production-first ops: rollout controls, KV caching, cost-aware tooling, and unified experience across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. essentially less ops work for you and clearer cost levers.
[15:52] Ethan: Also we like the ability to bring our own model and KMS control.

[17:00] [17:20] Liam: ok on pilot success criteria — propose: 1) p95 latency under 350ms for chat on 512 tokens, 2) embeddings throughput 10k/day with average latency <120ms, 3) cost reduction >25% versus current baseline, 4) security checklist passed (SOC2 docs, KMS configured). agree?
[17:48] Rajiv: those look good. we'll add a quality check on model outputs (no regression vs our test prompts).
[18:00] Samira: perfect. next steps — we'll share the kickoff runbook, security pack, and pilot pricing.

[20:00] [20:25] Priya: scheduling notes: Liam will run infra intake, Samira sends docs, Ethan sends traces. we'll do a threat model with Sofia.

[21:30] [22:00] Maya: one more infra detail — do you support peering to multiple accounts across AWS orgs? we use multiple accounts for prod/staging.
[22:10] Liam: yes supported — we can peer multiple accounts or use cross-account roles; we will detail options.

[25:00] [25:40] Ethan: any gotchas on tokenization differences across models that affect billing?
[25:50] Liam: yes tokenization variance occurs; Console shows token counts per model. for cost comparison we recommend normalizing to a single model family and doing evals on your prompts.

[30:00] [30:12] Rajiv: procurement question — what's typical contract length for Dedicated?
[30:20] Samira: Dedicated is typically monthly or annual reserved capacity with commit discounts. pilot usually uses short-term committed pilot pricing. we'll share pricing tiers.

[34:00] [34:20] Sofia: audit logging — can logs be exported to our SIEM?
[34:28] Liam: yes, audit logs and request metadata can be pushed to your SIEM via forwarders. for Private you can keep logs in your cluster entirely.

[38:00] [38:25] Ethan: engineering touchpoints — who will be our main support during pilot?
[38:32] Priya: Priya is CS lead. Liam is technical lead for infra. Samira is commercial. we'll add a Slack channel and weekly syncs.

[42:00] [42:18] Grace: would you run a couple of sample benchmarks — say 100 concurrent users for chat to see p95 under our traces?
[42:28] Liam: yes we can run benchmark in our staging cluster; we'll need your sample traffic and seq lengths. we'll run both hosted and dedicated variants for comparison.

[46:00] [46:30] Rajiv: any legal concerns for EU regulated PII? we may need DPA addendum.
[46:37] Samira: we have DPA templates and data residency clauses; legal team can follow up. I'll loop in sales ops.

[50:00] [50:15] Maya: timeline recap — I'll aim to deliver VPC topology by 12/12, Ethan will deliver traces by 12/10, Samira will send docs by 12/09.

[55:00] [55:20] Samira: Awesome. final quick recap — items and owners, we'll set weekly check-ins and a standing infra intake workshop. any final questions?
[55:32] Sofia: no further, thanks.
[55:40] Rajiv: thanks all. excited to get started.
[58:00] [58:45] Samira: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and deliverables.

End of transcript.
